title: Three Categories Of Teachers
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin sorts teachers into three categories based on their relationship to classroom management: those who prioritize it from the start and build long, joyful careers; those who are forced into prioritizing it after early struggles and successfully transform through hard-won study; and those who never make the shift and remain chronically stressed, often blaming students, parents, or administration rather than their own approach. Written as a follow-up to a piece about not quitting teaching, he acknowledges the piece risks sounding harsh but insists the stakes justify it. He closes with an extended call to action, pointing to his newly released book, The Smart Classroom Management Way, as a comprehensive resource for readers who want to move out of category three.
points: Defines three teacher categories: those who prioritize classroom management from the outset, those forced into prioritizing it after early struggle, and those who never make the shift.
Argues category-three teachers often misattribute their struggles to students, parents, administration, or 'just having a chatty bunch.'
States that transformation into category one or two is available to any teacher who studies and consistently applies real strategies.
Frames classroom management as the single area of teaching most responsible for a teacher's joy, peace, and effectiveness.
Promotes his newly released book, The Smart Classroom Management Way, as a unified resource distilling a decade of strategies.
quotes: No single area of teaching comes remotely close to providing the joy, the peace, and the effectiveness every teacher desires.
They are the small cadre of experts that leap out of bed in the morning and grow bored during the summer months.
They assume that it’s just how things are or buy into the myth that their problems lie with the students, parents, school, or administration.
You have to stop bribing students, trying to convince them to behave, or believing that you just have a chatty bunch—as if you’re at their mercy.
If you put what you learn into practice, and remain consistent, you’ll not only see stunning results almost immediately, but you’ll be on your way to the long, happy career you’ve always wanted.
